13.1 INTRODUCTION
It is important to press a garment for it to look good. However well a garment may have
been made, the final finished look comes only after pressing it. Tailors even press the fabric
at various stages during garment making. There are some garments whose cut components
have to be individually pressed. Garments like pant and shirt need to be pressed at each
.stage of construction. After the garment is ready, it is finally pressed and then folded and
packed. Hence, one must have adequate knowledge of all three stages of pressing, folding
and packing.
13.2
OBJECTIVES
After reading this lesson, you will be able to :
•
explain the need for pressing;
•
observe precautions while pressing;

. take adequate c.arewhile folding and packing.
3.4
NEED
As mentioned earlier, the final finishing of any garment is done by pressing. This makes
the garment took attractive. Pressing is essential because -

1..
It saves time
,
\
The fabric which is bought from the market is usually creased. Ifthe garment is
made from this creased cloth, we will waste time in opening and redoingthe seams
when the fitting is not proper. Hence it is better to remove all creases from the
cloth by ironing it before cutting. Ironing is also done where tacking is done, for
example, when folding for a hem, the cloth can be pressed while itis being evenly
folded. In this way one can save time while hemming and the work will also be
neater.
2.
It gives a neat finish
Minor defects in stitchingcan easilybe removed by pressing. The seams are pressed
into place and this gives the garment a neat finish.
,,
13. ,
It gives a complete took
There a:e some garments which are fitted at some places, loose at other places
and a tension is given at some places. Without pressing, a good fitting cannot be
achieved, nor do the gathers fall properly. It is only when the garment is pressed
that a compete, attractive look is obtained. Hence pressing a garment after making
it is an essential step.

,13.4 PRECAUTIONS WHILE PRESSING
It is essential to press the garment in order to give it a good shape. There are many
processes in dress making like -cutting is a process, binding is another, finishing edges is
another process. At every step, one needs to press.
;

garments. One needs to haveknowledge

should be observed while pressing:
•
1.
Before pressing, test the press on a waste piece,of cloth to see whether the sole
ofthepress
is rusted or not. Ifthe sole is rusted, clean the rust with a piece of
wax and then press the garment.
2.
Check to see that the press is pot dusty or dirty otherwise the garment will be.
soiled. Always keep the press clean.
3.
Check to ~eethe electrical wires ofthe press. Ifthere is a leak of current, get it

The temperature and weight of the press should be according to the requirement
ofthe garment. Some garments need a heavy press and some need a light press.
The same is the case with temperature.
7.
Set the temperature regulator on an automatic press according to the fabric of the
/
garment.
8.
Keep the basin of water on the right hand side and in a place so that it does not
splash.
9.
Rest the press on an iron stand. Ifthe press table has a stand for the.press, place
a piece of asbestos on it while using it.
10.
Do not sprinkle water on the garment. Ifneeded, moisten the fabric with a sponge.
11.
Use asoft, dry piece of mulmul when pressing over the metallic parts of garments.
Never press them without covering otherwise they win be tarnished.
12.
Press the seams from the wrong side of the garment when pressing during stitching.
13.
Place awet cloth over woollen garments while pressing otherwise the soft fibers
will get burnt.
. 14:-
Piled fabric should be pressed with a steam press or by pinning on aneedle board.
They should be pressed keeping the right sides facing.
,
15.
Woollen garments should be brushed to get rid of the dust before pressing. A wet
cloth should be placed over the gaiment while pressing.
16.
The person doing pressing should always wear rubber slippers or stand on a
wooden board. This prevents the possibility of an electric shock.
17.
The person doing pressing should always keep the hand dry.

2.
Place the press in its proper place after cooling it.
3.
Check the press and wires before putting it away.
4.
Never put away a hot press inan almirah.

13.5
FOLDING AND PACKING·
Every garment needs to be folded properly after pressing. If the garment is to be used at
home it can be hung up on a hanger. But for garments which have to be sent to be sold
in the market or which have to be handed over to the customer, foldingbecomes anecessity.
13.6 NEED
1.
The garment does not become crushed if it is properly folded after pressing.
2.
The garment looks presentable and attractive.
3.
A folded garment takes up less space.
4.
It is easy to transport folded garments to the market.
S.
Folded garment can be easily stored for long periods.
Various garments are folded in various ways, e.g. upper body garments and lower body
garments,
i)
Upper body garments
a)·
Gentsshirt
A cardboard or plastic piece in the shape of a band is inserted below the fold of
the collar-this holds up the collar and maintains the shape. Taking the neck point
-
and the center point of the arm hole as the base, both sides are folded back and
then both the sleeves are properly folded over so that the collar is properly visible.

Folding and Pressing Garments :: 127
b)
Ladies shirt
The entire shirt is first pressed properly and then the sides are folded back along
the crease line. The sleeves are then folded and set over the folded part of the
shirt. The shirt isthen folded in half, crease lines are properly set and the shirt is
then packed.
ii)
Lower body garments
The inner and outer seams are kept to.gether and the crease is set by pressing. If
the garment is to be packed in boxes, then a three fold is made length wise and
the garment packed in polythene bags and put into boxes.
13.7
PRECAUTIONS
WIDLE FOLDING
The following precautions must be observed while folding:
1.
A cardboard or plastic band should be used under the collar while folding a gents
shirt.
2.
The crease should not be disturbed while folding.
3.
The garment should have uniform creases.
4.
The garment should be folded only after proper pressing.
5.
Every garment should first be folded widthwise and then folded twice or thrice
lengthwise, as may be required.
6.
The neckline part of the garment should be on the front.
7.
The garment should not be unnecessarily folded at any part while packing.
8.
A garment needs to be folded more if it is to be packed in a box and it needs less
folds if it is to be packed in a polythene bag.
9.
A paper or cardboard should be used while foldingchildren garments.
10.
A garment should be properly packed after folding.
